acceptance.text: The codex lane's tool-call ceiling follows the invocation budget instead of a fixed five minutes. Today internal/driver/native_linux.go:2883 writes the literal `tool_timeout_sec = 300` into the [mcp_servers.sworn] TOML block that nativeConfigFiles (native_linux.go:2846-2887) builds for every codex invocation regardless of that invocation's own budget, and grep across every *_test.go file in the repository finds zero references to tool_timeout_sec - the value is untested. After this slice tool_timeout_sec is floor(MaxTimeoutMillis / 1000) seconds (86400, from MaxTimeoutMillis=86_400_000 at contract.go:32), so a codex worker's tool call is bounded by the same day-long ceiling the claude lane already grants via MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT/MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT (native_environment_linux.go:13,30-31). Pinned by a unit test that calls nativeConfigFiles for ProfileCodex and asserts the rendered mcp config's tool_timeout_sec line equals that derived value, not the literal 300.

The codex seconds value and the claude milliseconds value both read from the same MaxTimeoutMillis constant at contract.go:32: today native_linux.go:2883's literal `300` and native_environment_linux.go:13's `nativeMCPToolTimeoutMillis = strconv.FormatInt(MaxTimeoutMillis, 10)` are two independent numbers with no relationship to each other - one already tracks MaxTimeoutMillis, the other is a bare literal someone must remember to update by hand. After this slice codex's tool_timeout_sec is derived the same way, from the same constant, as a second reader alongside native_environment_linux.go:13. Pinned by a unit test that generates both a codex config and a claude environment for the same invocation and asserts the codex tool_timeout_sec value (seconds) times 1000 equals the claude MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT value (millis) - this proves the two current outputs agree numerically for that invocation, it does not and cannot prove a worker could never reintroduce a second independent literal that happens to match; no Go test pins that implementation-coupling property, only the observable value agreement.

startup_timeout_sec stays 5 and the rest of the codex TOML block - model_catalog_json, web_search, include_permissions_instructions, include_apps_instructions, include_collaboration_mode_instructions, include_environment_context, and the [analytics]/[agents]/[orchestrator.*]/[skills.*] toggles at native_linux.go:2846-2887 - is byte-identical apart from the tool_timeout_sec line; this is an additive, single-value fix, not a rewrite of the config surface the in-sandbox certificate already checks (runtime.codex_config_capability_count at native_linux.go:2681-2686 counts capability-token occurrences in the joined config bytes and is unaffected by a numeric-literal change elsewhere in the same file). Pinned by a unit test that calls nativeConfigFiles for ProfileCodex with a fixed invocation/capability/brokerURL and asserts the rendered mcp TOML string equals an expected-template string built from today's full literal block with only the tool_timeout_sec value substituted - one full string-equality assertion, not two narrow spot checks - so a dropped, reordered, or altered key anywhere in the other seven lines fails the test; the existing nativeConfigFiles/native-surface coverage in native_linux_test.go continues to pass unmodified on its capability-count assertions.

constraints: No behaviour change for any tool call that finishes inside five minutes: this slice only raises the ceiling a codex tool call may run before the MCP server itself enforces a timeout, it does not touch how or when a call is dispatched, retried, or reported.

No new magic numbers: the only two places a tool-call timeout may be expressed are the existing MaxTimeoutMillis constant at contract.go:32 and values derived from it in native_linux.go and native_environment_linux.go - no second literal budget is introduced for either lane.

The capability bearer token must still appear exactly once in the generated codex config (runtime.codex_config_capability_count, native_linux.go:2681-2686) after the change - this slice only alters the tool_timeout_sec line's value, never the TOML block's structure or where the capability token is interpolated.
No secret, credential, or capability token is ever printed in a test assertion or added log line; existing redaction and canary discipline in native_linux_test.go is unchanged.

This is additive and single-purpose: startup_timeout_sec, every other codex TOML key, the default/ProfileClaude branches of the switch config.Family block in nativeConfigFiles (native_linux.go:2843-2891), and the claude lane's MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT/MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT wiring are unmodified except for gaining the codex lane as a second reader of the same constant.

The two go test checks are declared as host_checks: the engine runs them on the host (a 60-minute budget each) and records host_effect evidence, because sworn's own suite cannot complete inside a worker sandbox - there is no C toolchain there so -race cannot build, and cmd/sworn's tests start sandboxes of their own. The vet and gofmt checks stay in-turn. A verifier must not attempt the go test checks itself and must not treat their absence from its own turn as uncovered evidence.
